verdict.rationale: AWS documents per-service, date-stamped API versions carried on every request (for example EC2 2016-11-15), and the published machine models are keyed to those versions. It also publishes a service lifecycle policy with Maintenance, Sunset, and Full Shutdown stages and a typical 12-month sunset timeline. However, that policy covers whole services and features, not API versions, and AWS commits to no per-API-version deprecation window. Missing for 10: a deprecation policy or window tied to specific API versions, a platform-wide versioning document, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on versioned APIs with a documented deprecation policy

citations.quote: **Version**: The API version to use. For the Amazon EC2 API, the version is 2016-11-15.
Sunset services have a sunset time line (typically 12 months).
At AWS, we use Smithy extensively to model our service APIs and provide the daily releases of the AWS SDKs and CLIs
